# Digest meeting notes: Airtable & Notion

**Pattern:** AI Summarize & Route · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers knowledge-sync work end to end across Airtable, Notion, Discord and Slack.

It moves through 28 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Read Recent from Notion
3. Newest First
4. Trim to Digest Size
5. Summarize Content (AI)
6. Groq Chat Model
7. Post Digest to Discord
8. Archive Digest in Airtable
9. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
10. Archive Row Snapshot
11. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
12. Record Sub-workflow Result
13. Stamp Completion Time
14. Persist Run Metadata
15. Fingerprint for Idempotency
16. Drop Already-Processed Items
17. Load Previous Snapshot
18. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
19. Enrich with Reference Data
20. Fold In Enrichment Fields
21. Sort Documents Newest First
22. Save Execution Metadata
23. Guard Non-Empty title
24. Align Field Names
25. Cap Batch Volume
26. Summarize Run Stats
27. Append Audit Row (Notion)
28. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing knowledge-sync work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Read Recent from Notion → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → Groq Chat Model → Post Digest to Discord → Archive Digest in Airtable → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Sort Documents Newest First → Save Execution Metadata → Guard Non-Empty title → Align Field Names → Cap Batch Volume → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Discord → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Airtable and Notion aligned by hand for knowledge sync
- Pushing knowledge-sync events into Airtable and Notion the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Knowledge sync work where "Read Recent from Notion" is still a manual step before Airtable
- Knowledge sync work that only reaches Airtable when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Airtable and Notion in step for knowledge sync, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Airtable or Notion are skipped, across all 31 nodes of this knowledge-sync build
- A failed Airtable or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 31 nodes in this knowledge-sync build
- Every knowledge-sync run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Airtable
- The knowledge-sync AI step is isolated from Airtable, so models swap without touching the other 31 nodes

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Airtable PAT; Discord webhook URL; Groq API key; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Groq API key**
console.groq.com → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Very fast and cheap, but with tight per-minute rate limits.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy URL.
_Gotcha:_ Webhook mode needs no bot token. Messages cap at 2000 characters.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Discord: give the bot access to the destination channel only, not the whole guild.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole knowledge-sync payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your knowledge sync process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
